question: For a potential stop condition on a 55-mph approach, what advance placement distance is shown in Table 2C-3, and should it be treated as an inflexible mandatory distance?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a 55-mph posted or 85th-percentile speed, Table 2C-3 lists 495 feet for the potential stop condition (Condition B, deceleration to 0 mph — the column used for Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, and Signal Ahead signs). This distance is a guideline, not an inflexible mandate: Table 2C-3 is presented as "Guidelines for Advance Placement of Warning Signs" and the distances should be applied with engineering judgment and adjusted as needed (e.g., a minimum of 100 feet should be added for signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words). However, in certain contexts (e.g., at passive grade crossings) the MUTCD does mandate locating the Stop Ahead/Yield Ahead sign in accordance with Table 2C-3. Standards (mandatory): - "The Stop Ahead (W3-1), Yield Ahead (W3-2), and Signal Ahead (W3-3) Advance Traffic Control signs (see Figure 2C-8) shall be installed on an approach to a primary traffic control device that is not visible for a sufficient distance to permit the road user to respond to the device (see Table 2C-3)." - At passive grade crossings with a YIELD or STOP sign: "The Yield Ahead or Stop Ahead sign shall be located in accordance with Table 2C-3. The minimum distance between the signs shall be in accordance with Section 2C.04 and Table 2C-3." Guidance (recommended): - Table 2C-3 shows, for 55 mph, 495 ft under the Condition B "0 mph" column (the potential stop condition); the table is titled "Guidelines for Advance Placement of Warning Signs," indicating recommended rather than mandatory distances. - "For Conditions A and B, warning signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words, a minimum of 100 feet should be added to the advance placement distance to provide adequate legibility of the warning sign." - "The effectiveness of the placement of warning signs should be periodically evaluated under both day and night conditions." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2C-3 shows the 55 mph row with 495 ft in the "0³" column, and footnote 3 identifies this column as the potential stop condition (typical signs: Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, Signal Ahead, and Intersection Warning), based on 2018 AASHTO stopping sight distance with a 2.5-second PRT and deceleration of 11.2 feet/second². - [Image 2] Page 152 shows Section 2C.04, whose Guidance states that the distances in Table 2C-3 "should be applied with engineering judgment" and that the distances "can be adjusted for roadway features, other signing, and to improve visibility," confirming the table is not an inflexible mandate. - [Image 3] Page 189 (Figure 2C-13, Sheet 5) illustrates use of the table with the annotation "See Table 2C-3 to determine the advance placement distance" for a lane-merge warning sign. - [Image 4] Page 185 (Figure 2C-13, Sheet 1) similarly annotates "See Table 2C-3 to determine the advance placement distance" for a W4-2R lane ends sign. - [Image 5] Page 156 (Figure 2C-2) notes "See Table 2C-3 for advance placement distance guidelines," reinforcing the guideline character of the table. Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.35 Standard §1 (p.177) - Section 8B.06 Standard §3 (p.1001)
gold_answer: The table shows 495 feet. It is a guideline to be applied with engineering judgment and may be adjusted for roadway features, other signing, and visibility; it is not an inflexible universal mandate.
